To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the carboxyl-terminal domains of NF-H and M subunits are not required for the transport of NF, but are required for maintaining the content of NF in axons by stabilizing the stationary NF cytoskeleton.
the carboxyl-terminal domains of NF-H and M subunits maintain the content of the stationary NF network by preventing proteolytic turnover of NF in the stationary network.

deletion of both NF-H and NF- M C-terminal domains selectively lowers NF protein content along optic axons of NF-(H/M)tai1Δ mice without altering either rates or slow axonal transport or NF subunit synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms that maintain the structural integrity of the axon, the longest and most highly differentiated cell in the body.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate axonal transport of neurofilaments and the stability of the stationary cytoskeleton along the axons of neurons.
how neurofilaments, a major component of the neuronal cytoskeleton, are transported and maintained in the axon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NF-H and NF–M carboxy-terminal tail domains are required to maintain the axonal neurofilament network by protecting it from degradation.
the NF-H and NF/M C-terminal tails are not required for axonal transport of neurofilaments but instead are required to stabilize neurofilaments in the stationary cytoskeleton of axons.

NF-H and -M C-terminal domains do indeed stabilize the stationary NF cytoskeleton along the length of axons by increasing the proteolytic stability of the NF network, and thereby maintain NF levels in the axon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-terminal domains of the neurofilament subunits NF-H and NF–M stabilize the stationary cytoskeleton of neurofilaments in axons by blocking proteolytic turnover of the cytoskeleton.
NF-H and M C-terminal domains are required for the maintenance of axonal neurofilament content by blocking turnover of the stationary neurofilaments.
the C-terminal domains of NF-H and M are required to maintain a high level of NF in the axon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-terminal domains of NF-H and -M subunits maintain axonal neurofilament content by slowing the rate of turnover of the stationary neurofilaments in axons.
the C-terminal domains of NF-H and M, and not the phosphorylation status of these domains, are critical to maintaining the stability of the stationary NF network in axons.

the carboxyl-terminal domains of the heavy (NF-H) and medium (NF-M) neurofilament (NFL) subunits do not regulate neurofilament transport along axons, but instead maintain the stability of the stationary neurofilaments by blocking their turnover.
